evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/push_fanout.rs:280 and :773 — the FCM and APNs transport adapters build their reqwest client with `reqwest::Client::builder()...build().expect("reqwest client build should not fail")`. `reqwest::ClientBuilder::build()` returns a `Result` precisely because it can fail (TLS backend initialization; the APNs adapter also pins `http2_prior_knowledge()`), so this `expect` is a panic path, not a guaranteed-infallible unwrap.

Reachability: `FcmHttpAdapter::new` / `ApnsHttpAdapter::new` are called at server startup via `FcmHttpAdapter::from_env` / `ApnsHttpAdapter::from_env` -> `CombinedPushAdapter::new` (push_fanout.rs:1061-1062, 1293) -> `PushFanoutWorker::new` (main.rs:695). A build failure therefore aborts the whole api-server process during boot.

Inconsistency with the module's own stated design: `CombinedPushAdapter::new` deliberately degrades gracefully when push is unconfigured — the surrounding code logs `"neither FCM nor APNs is configured; push delivery will be skipped (no crash — set env vars to enable)"` (push_fanout.rs:1285-1289). Panicking on a transport-client build failure contradicts that never-crash-the-server-over-push contract. Fix: make `new`/`from_env` return `Result` (or fall back to a disabled/no-op transport with a `tracing::error!`) instead of `.expect(...)`, so an infrastructure-level reqwest build error degrades push delivery rather than taking down the whole server. Low severity: build failures are rare and only at startup, but the crash path is real and avoidable.

Scope note: the rest of the reviewed api-core segment (churn hotspot services/scheduler.rs, plus services/oauth.rs, services/stripe.rs, services/jwt.rs, services/totp.rs, services/workflow_executor.rs, services/auth.rs) is robustly defended — poison-safe mutex locks (`lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())`), guarded RLS/global-read context teardown via `release_scheduler_conn`, atomic OAuth code find-and-consume, mandatory S256 PKCE, Stripe webhook HMAC via constant-time `ct_eq`, no secrets in logs, and no production-path `unwrap`/`todo!`/`unsafe`. No medium/high findings in this pass.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/integrations/install.rs:1061 and :1065 (fn sync_booking, line 1007) — Booking.com OTA credentials are read as `integrations::decrypt_if_available(crypto.as_ref(), &connection.access_token.clone().unwrap_or_default())` for the username and `refresh_token.clone().unwrap_or_default()` for the password. When the connection row has NULL access/refresh tokens, `unwrap_or_default()` yields an empty string, so a `BookingCredentials::new(hotel_id, "", "")` is built and a live OTA API call is made with blank credentials.

Inconsistency in the same handler: the required `external_property_id` immediately above (line 1045) is handled correctly with `.ok_or_else(|| (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, ErrorResponse::new("NOT_CONFIGURED", "Hotel ID not configured")))`. Missing OTA credentials should surface the same clean 400 NOT_CONFIGURED, but instead they fall through to an opaque upstream auth failure (or a generic 500) that hides the real 'credentials not configured' cause from the manager triggering the sync.

Repeated in two sibling Booking OTA handlers: install.rs:1381/:1385 (fn push_booking_availability, line 1318) and install.rs:1529 (fn push_booking_rates, line 1466) use the identical `access_token.clone().unwrap_or_default()` / `refresh_token.clone().unwrap_or_default()` pattern. Fix: replace the three `unwrap_or_default()` credential reads with an `ok_or_else(... NOT_CONFIGURED ...)` guard mirroring the hotel_id check, so a partially-configured connection fails fast with a clear 400 instead of attempting an OTA call with empty credentials.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth.rs:~2324 (GET /me) and :~2416 (profile update response) compute the response flag as `two_factor_enabled = state.two_factor_repo.get_by_user_id(user.id).await.ok().flatten().map(|r| r.enabled).unwrap_or(false)`. The `.ok()` swallows any DB error and the `.unwrap_or(false)` then reports 2FA as DISABLED whenever the lookup transiently fails, even for a user who actually has 2FA enabled.

This is a display/state-reporting flag only (login-time enforcement reads the record independently and fails closed at auth.rs:~800 where TOTP `verify_code(...).unwrap_or(false)` denies on error), so it is NOT a security bypass — but on a transient DB blip the account page and the profile-update response can tell the user 2FA is off when it is on, which is misleading and could prompt a redundant/erroneous re-enrollment. Low severity. Fix: distinguish a genuine `Ok(None)` (no record -> false) from an `Err(_)` (DB failure -> propagate 500 or retain last-known state) instead of collapsing both to `false`.

Scope note: the rest of the reviewed api-handlers churn hotspots are robustly defended. Document public-share access (routes/documents/shares.rs access_shared_document/access_protected_share) enforces expiry + revocation in SQL (`revoked_at IS NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > NOW())` in find_share_by_token_rls), share passwords are argon2-hashed (repositories/document/internal.rs hash_password), revoke is IDOR-hardened with a document_id predicate (#2197), integrations/sync.rs releases the RLS connection on every early-return branch, and integrations/webhook.rs verifies Stripe HMAC signatures and its `Ok(StatusCode::OK)` early returns are all intentional, commented webhook-ack paths. No security or crash-path findings in this pass.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/agent_reviews.rs:190-266 — the public `create_review` handler validates only `rating` (1..=5, line 196) and then binds the user-controlled `data.body` straight into `INSERT INTO realtor_reviews (... body ...)` at line 265. There is NO maximum-length check and NO non-empty/trim check on `body` (grep for `body` + `len|MAX|empty|trim|valid` in the file returns nothing).

This is inconsistent with every sibling public write path in the same segment, which all enforce input bounds: routes/inquiries.rs caps message at MAX_INQUIRY_MESSAGE_LEN=5000 via validate_inquiry_lengths (lines 24-52, enforced at 188-190), and routes/reports.rs caps description at MAX_REPORT_DESCRIPTION_LEN=5000 (lines 27, 161-166). agent_reviews.rs is the lone public write endpoint with an unbounded free-text field.

Impact (missing input validation on an internet-facing, authenticated-but-public write path): an attacker with any portal account can POST an arbitrarily large `body` (bounded only by the request-body limit) and persist it — storage bloat / DB row-size pressure and unbounded payload echoed back on the public list_reviews GET (lines 80-160). Empty/whitespace-only reviews are also accepted. Fix: add a MAX_REVIEW_BODY_LEN constant (mirror the 5000 used by inquiries/reports), reject over-length and empty/whitespace-only bodies with 400 BAD_REQUEST before the INSERT, matching the existing validate_inquiry_lengths pattern.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/services/saved_search_alerts.rs:237 — the saved-search enqueue worker advances the per-search watermark with `let _ = self.repo.mark_saved_search_matched(&mut *conn, search.id, ids.len() as i64).await;`, silently discarding the Result. If this DB write fails AFTER a successful `enqueue_search_alert` (line 216), `last_matched_at` is not advanced, so on the next due poll `find_new_match_listing_ids(.., Some(since), ..)` recomputes the SAME window (unchanged `since`) and re-enqueues the SAME listing IDs, producing a duplicate saved-search alert email/push to the user.

Same file line 176 — the first-sighting watermark write (`let _ = self.repo.mark_saved_search_matched(&mut *conn, search.id, 0).await;`) is also swallowed; if it fails the search never establishes its baseline and will re-enter the first-sighting branch every poll, so it never starts alerting.

Observability gap / inconsistency: every sibling error path in this same file uses structured logging (tracing::error at 166, tracing::warn at 194 and 205 and 227), and the parallel workers services/search_alert_drainer.rs (run_once, tracing::error on mark_search_alert_notified failure at ~321) and services/favorite_alerts.rs (tracing::warn on every pass failure, lines 121/133) log all DB failures. saved_search_alerts.rs is the lone place that drops the mark-matched Result with no log, so a failing watermark write is invisible to operators AND causes duplicate/again-suppressed alerts.

Fix: replace both `let _ = ... mark_saved_search_matched(...).await;` with `if let Err(e) = ... { tracing::warn!(id = %search.id, error = %e, "[#983] failed to advance saved-search watermark"); }` (matching the enqueue-failure handling immediately above at line 227), so failures are observable and the retry semantics are intentional rather than silent.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/util/url_validator.rs:146-165 — the `Host::Ipv6` branch of `validate_fetch_url` only rejects `is_loopback()` (::1), `fc00::/7` and `fe80::/10`. It does NOT reject IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) or IPv4-compatible addresses. `std::net::Ipv6Addr::is_loopback` returns false for `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, and the fc00/fe80 masks never match `::ffff:...`, so a mapped address slips straight through as an allowed fetch URL.

This is a full SSRF-guard bypass: an attacker can encode any blocked IPv4 target as a mapped IPv6 literal to defeat the entire IPv4 blocklist (private ranges, 127.0.0.0/8, and crucially 169.254.169.254 cloud metadata). Example payloads: `https://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/latest/meta-data/`, `https://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/`, `https://[::ffff:10.0.0.5]/feed.xml`. Unlike `Host::Domain`, an IP literal is never re-resolved by the worker, so the documented 'worker re-validates resolved IP' defense does not apply here.

Reachability (traced end-to-end): user-controlled `feed_url` from agency-member requests reaches this guard at backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/agency_imports.rs:238 (test_connection) and :290 (run_import); both call `validate_fetch_url(url)` as the only pre-fetch SSRF gate (marked SECURITY H3, round-9 audit). Fix: after matching `Host::Ipv6`, canonicalize via `ip.to_ipv4_mapped()` / `to_ipv4()` and re-run the IPv4 blocklist on the embedded address; also reject the unspecified address `::`.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:148-151 — `check_redirect_uri_allowed` treats any value starting with `/` (but not `//`) as an unconditionally-allowed same-origin relative path: `if raw.starts_with('/') && !raw.starts_with("//") { return Ok(()); }`. This only blocks the protocol-relative `//evil.com` form, not the backslash variant `/\evil.com` (or `/\/evil.com`).

Chrome and Firefox normalize backslashes to forward slashes when resolving a Location URL, so the browser resolves `/\evil.com` to `//evil.com` = protocol-relative → navigates to https://evil.com. This is an open-redirect bypass on the SSO redirect_uri allowlist (the value is threaded through the OAuth `state` and used as the post-login redirect target). Open redirect on an auth-callback endpoint is a common phishing / token-leak primitive.

Fix: after the leading-slash fast path, also reject values whose second character is `\` (and normalize backslashes before the `//` check), or drop the relative-path fast path and require every redirect_uri to parse and match the allowlist explicitly.
